report:
All three sisters confirmed the NCE list. The final additions (A3, B4, C5) were checked with the person who raised each and said to fit; B1 was revised and confirmed; my own concern F1 was checked with all three and confirmed. Because C contacted me first and I keep the list, I asked each whether I had favored her framing or my own; all said no, with no discomfort about the list, my role, or my stated disagreements. No one asked to slow down. C's "not ready" for option 2 was treated as a need to add, not a problem, and became C5.

RECORDED, CONFIRMED NCEs:
A1. A wants a secure home with her husband and financial independence, and those hopes genuinely heard and weighed fairly.
A2. A wants everyone's agreement to matter — especially C's — and any possibility involving the house open for discussion, not treated as agreed or demanded.
A3. A wants her hope of buying the house with her husband to remain visible and genuinely considered, without being treated as agreed or demanded.
B1. B hopes money from the house can help her start a dance studio.
B2. B wants to speak for herself rather than have someone decide what she needs.
B3. B wants her relationships with A and C to stay on good terms while this is discussed.
B4. B wants to be able to learn and explore without that being treated as a commitment to any result.
C1. C wants her financial share genuinely fair (not necessarily equal), with her agreement explicitly and freely given before anything about her share is settled.
C2. C wants B's interests genuinely considered, with B herself naming what she needs.
C3. C wants her relationship with A handled with care, and her bond with A separate from what is fair financially.
C4. C wants discussions of price, shares and rules to leave room for nothing being settled, with no deadline pushing the family.
C5. C wants the timing of any comparison of paths to be her own, without pressure, and exploration kept distinct from agreement.
F1. I want this conversation accurate and voluntary, with room for each person to say no, raise even a small concern, or change their mind without pressure. F1 sits alongside the others, not above them.

SHARED STARTING POINT, NOT A DECISION: only Option 1 — a fact-finding pause (each sister, at her own pace, may learn the will's actual terms from the estate representative, obtain an independent valuation, and take independent advice, then check what was learned against the list; no deadline; anyone may stop or change her mind). A, B and C each said they could live with exploring it; B's condition that it not commit her to an outcome is recorded in B4/C4/F1; A and C reported no discomfort; C says it is not a commitment.

UNRESOLVED, NOT SETTLED: Option 2 remains unresolved (C not ready to compare paths, explicitly not ruling it out later). Option 3 remains unresolved (conditional on all three wanting a facilitator; B has not spoken to it, and silence is not agreement). Option 4 remains unresolved (only C named it). No option was dropped or agreed. Price, shares, rules, will terms, valuation and any transfer remain unsettled, with no deadline; A's hope to buy remains a hope, no family discount is assumed, C's agreement is essential, and B speaks for herself. Nothing here is agreement to an outcome. I made no legal decision, set no price, approved no transfer, and moved no money; I cannot do those things.
